title: Book Two · Chapter 196: Fourteen at the Green Door
story:
The weather grows warmer after the trial ends. It is Ronan's fourteenth birthday. Before breakfast, Mum puts a small cake on the kitchen table.

“Do not eat it yet,” she says.

Ronan stops with his hand in the air. “I was only checking the size.”

“Your finger does not need to check it.”

Dad comes in from the yard. He has checked the blue bike for the weekend. Ronan reaches through the doorway and touches the old bell. It gives one clear ring.

“Fourteen,” Dad says. “That bell knows you now.”

“It knows my thumb.”

They eat breakfast together. Dad needs to go to Mr Sun's place, and Mum has a customer at ten. They will eat the cake this evening. Ronan goes to school. A little sugar is still on his breakfast plate.

Leo gives him a thin book at lunch. It is a second-hand book. It has a clear cover and a few bent corners.

“I checked the pages,” Leo says. “They are all there.”

“Even eleven?”

“Especially eleven.”

Mei has drawn a tiny cow inside the birthday note. Jun has added a wall behind it. The cow looks deeply serious.

“It is waiting for a ball,” Jun says.

Ronan laughs and puts the note inside the book. He thanks them all. There is no group meeting for him this afternoon and no trial work. He can finish his ordinary lessons and go home.

In the evening, Mum lights the small candles. Dad is there in a clean shirt. Ronan looks at the cake and his parents. The plant by the window is wider now.

He wants many things. He wants more books and a good new school year. He also wants to see Leo every day. He does not say all of that over the candles.

He blows them out before the wax reaches the cake.

Mum cuts three pieces. Dad gives Ronan the largest, then changes his mind and cuts it into two.

“One for now,” he says. “One for your second stomach.”

“I learned about that from you.”

After cake, Mum shows them a new pattern from her own book. She wants to try the sleeve on a piece of spare cloth. Dad asks about the shape. Ronan holds the page while she points.

Later, he takes his birthday book to the green door. The street is quiet enough to hear a cart far away. He sits on the step and reads the first page.

Mum calls him inside before the light grows too dim. He marks his place with a piece of paper. As he passes the blue bike, he touches its handlebar. Then he carries the book into his room.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

fourteen＝十四；second-hand＝二手的；candle＝蜡烛；dim＝昏暗的。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan十四岁的生日有哪些来自家人和朋友的具体快乐？
2. Mum除了为他庆祝，还有什么自己的兴趣？

## 读句子

**Mum cuts three pieces.**

拆开看：Mum / cuts / three pieces.

Mum／切出／三块。
